Record source-artifact identity for DB primitives

Source: R/lnk_artifact.R
lnk_artifact_record.Rd

Upserts rows into provenance.source_artifact, the table that says which version of which object each primitive in this database was loaded from (link#265). The bchamp object store is versioned but cannot be listed, so a version id not recorded at load time is gone for good; this is where it is recorded.

Usage

lnk_artifact_record(
  conn,
  artifacts,
  recorded_by = c("loader", "probe"),
  host = .lnk_host()
)

Arguments

conn

A DBI::DBIConnection to the database the primitives live in.

artifacts

A data frame with table_name and url, and optionally version_id, etag, last_modified, loaded_at and notes. kind is taken from the dictionary. last_modified may be POSIXct or the raw HTTP header string ("Thu, 16 Apr 2026 02:22:39 GMT").

recorded_by

"loader" or "probe".

host

Host label. Defaults to LNK_HOST_ALIAS, else the node name — the same label the run log uses.

Value

Invisibly, the rows as recorded (before the probe-vs-loader rule is applied by the database).

Details

recorded_by is the strength of the evidence. "loader" rows come from the thing that did the load (data-raw/snapshot_bcfp.sh pins each fetch to the version it records). "probe" rows come from a HEAD after the fact and say only that the version is current now. A probe never overwrites a loader row, so weaker evidence cannot replace stronger. Nor does a probe overwrite an earlier probe that named a different version while the table's row count is unchanged: the earlier probe was taken closer to the load, and the store moving on since says nothing about what is loaded here. A changed row count is taken as a reload, and the newer probe replaces it. A loader row always replaces whatever is there.

Every url must be one lnk_artifact_record() knows for that table — the primitives dictionary's URL, with {wsg} expanded. A loader that fetches from somewhere else stops here rather than recording an identity for an object the rest of link does not know about.

n_rows is counted from the database at record time: exactly, per watershed group for the per-group stream objects. A table that does not exist records n_rows NULL and says so in notes.

See also

Other provenance: lnk_artifact_probe(), lnk_artifact_read()

Examples

# Which artifacts the dictionary knows, without touching a database:
prims <- link:::.lnk_input_primitives()
prims[, c("table_name", "kind")]
#>                                            table_name    kind
#> 1             whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_sp  object
#> 2  whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_channel_width  object
#> 3      whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_discharge  object
#> 4   whse_basemapping.fwa_stream_networks_order_parent derived
#> 5                     whse_basemapping.fwa_lakes_poly  object
#> 6                  whse_basemapping.fwa_wetlands_poly  object
#> 7                    whse_basemapping.fwa_rivers_poly  object
#> 8                whse_basemapping.fwa_obstructions_sp  object
#> 9                              bcfishobs.observations  object
#> 10                     whse_fish.pscis_assessment_svw     api
#> 11                                          cabd.dams     api
#> 12                    fresh.modelled_stream_crossings  object

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
conn <- lnk_db_conn(dbname = "fwapg", host = "localhost", port = 5432L,
                    user = "postgres", password = "postgres")
lnk_artifact_record(conn, data.frame(
  table_name = "cabd.dams",
  url = prims$url[prims$table_name == "cabd.dams"],
  loaded_at = Sys.time()), recorded_by = "loader")
} # }
